What sort of hosting do you have it on? I see from the headers that you're using Cloudflare; does Cloudflare only load-balance/cache things, or does it also directly host the site?

*doesn't know what CloudFlare exactly offers.*

It's hosted on Amazon's Elastic Beanstalk, and I'm attempting to use CloudFlare as a CDN, both to reduce bandwidth costs and increase responsiveness. Problem is, EB's load balancer doesn't use a static IP, so I have to use cname records, which DNS doesn't support on a TLD, and it's making everything go crazy.

A redirect loop is incredibly strange though. Cloudflare shouldn't do that, and the only permanent redirect my server has is from www.veuwer.com to veuwer.com. I don't think that's a problem that DNS would cause.

Sooo I'm still figuring things out. Fun times.

I figured out why it was redirecting. There was an SSL setting from a previous time I tried cloudflare that took https connections and converted them to http so I didn't need my own certificate. I disabled cloudflare after that, got my own certificate, and added a redirect on the server from http to https. So when I enabled cloudflare again, it converted https connections to http, which the server redirected to https, which caused a new connection attempt that cloudflare converted to http....

Yeah that was a fun thing to debug.

Just figured you'd be interested in an update.

Hey, thanks for the update! That is kinda odd, but at the same time, I thought the headers were indicating that https was being redirected to https. Was it just that CloudFlare was taking care of one iteration of the 'loop' (due to caching or something)?

Well your https signal went to cloudflare, which it converted to http, then sent to the server, like a relay. The server returned a redirect to https. So yeah, from your perspective it would like you were being redirected from https. From the server's perspective, it was receiving an http connection and trying to make you switch to https.

Definitely confusing.
